create.name: Sufi Center Minnesota
create.bio:
Sufi Center Minnesota is a Sufi community in the Twin Cities area, based in Bloomington, that follows the Shadhiliyya order, a path known for its emphasis on the heart. Its lineage runs through Sidi Shaykh Muhammad al-Jamal of Jerusalem, who guided the order until his death in 2015 and travelled widely from the 1990s to teach seekers of every background. The community has gathered since 1998, and its teachers include ministers, educators and others who have trained for years on the Sufi path; among the teachers it welcomes is Dr Ibrahim Jaffe, a Murshid of the order.

The centre presents Sufism as the mystical heart of Islam while welcoming people of any faith or none, without asking them to leave their own tradition. Its approach rests on a few simple supports: a direct sense of the One, steady daily practice, letting go of what blocks the heart, service and community. Most gatherings are on Zoom, with some in person: weekly remembrance (dhikr), a Monday reading group, study of the Divine Names, chanting evenings, a monthly guest teaching and occasional fifth-Sunday gatherings. Recorded talks are shared on its website and YouTube, and most events are offered for donations.

free_resources.title: A Drop of the Love
free_resources.description: A weekly Monday-morning Zoom class (Central time) with Cindy Yasmine Rahmana Libman, reading a book on the Sufi path aloud from start to finish, with teaching and discussion. Registration brings links to earlier replays; all are welcome.

free_resources.title: Renewal Through Divine Chant
free_resources.description: An in-person Thursday-evening gathering every other week for spoken Sufi chants and sung chants from the wider Abrahamic tradition, using voice, breath and movement as prayer.

free_resources.title: Gathering in the Love: Special Fifth Sunday Topics
free_resources.description: A free Zoom gathering held on the occasional fifth Sunday of a month, built around a Sufi theme, with time for reflection, sharing and practical steps for daily life. Donations are welcome.
